$comment: Business plan narrative — the sections around the computed financial-projections table, which the engine renders separately (see projections-math.mjs and the businessplan-specific block in renderDoc). No clause here quotes a party role in curly quotes, on purpose, same reasoning as invoice.json: a business plan is not an agreement between two parties, signs no one, and needs no defined-term pair for terminology.mjs to check. Jurisdiction-neutral, drafting only — every judgement call (market size, competitors, staffing, assumptions behind the numbers) is a bracketed prompt for the business owner to fill in, never asserted here.

clauses.title: Executive Summary
clauses.rationale: Opens the plan with what the business is and why the reader should keep going, built directly from the one answer every business plan wizard run collects.
clauses.body: {{company}} is a business built around {{productDesc}}. This plan describes the opportunity, how {{company}} intends to pursue it, and what the numbers are expected to look like over the next few years.

clauses.title: Company Description
clauses.rationale: Founding story, structure and current stage are specific enough that no wizard answer should stand in for them — left as a clear bracketed prompt rather than guessed at.
clauses.body: [Describe when and why {{company}} was founded, its legal structure and location, and what stage the business is at today.]

clauses.title: Market Analysis
clauses.rationale: Uses the optional target-market answer when it was given, then still prompts for the market-sizing detail no short wizard answer can carry.
clauses.body: The target market is {{targetMarket}}. [Add market size, growth trends, and any research supporting the opportunity.]

clauses.title: Market Analysis
clauses.rationale: The no-target-market variant — the section still has to read cleanly as a labeled prompt rather than leaving a blank where an answer would go.
clauses.body: [Describe the target market: who the customer is, how large the market is, and why now.]

clauses.title: Competitive Analysis
clauses.rationale: Naming actual competitors and the real differentiation is a judgement call for the business owner, not something the wizard can infer from a package/industry pick.
clauses.body: [Identify the main competitors or alternatives, and explain what makes {{company}} different or better.]

clauses.title: Marketing & Sales Strategy
clauses.rationale: Channels, pricing approach and sales process vary too much by business to guess at from wizard answers.
clauses.body: [Describe how {{company}} will reach customers and convert them into paying customers — channels, pricing approach, and sales process.]

clauses.title: Management & Organization
clauses.rationale: Who is actually running the business and what gaps remain is real information a reader (lender, investor, co-founder) is going to ask about first.
clauses.body: [List the founders or leadership team, their relevant background, and any key roles still to be filled.]

clauses.title: Funding Request
clauses.rationale: Only appears when the wizard's optional funding question was answered — a plan that is not raising money should not carry a funding section at all.
clauses.body: {{company}} is seeking funding: {{fundingAsk}}. [Add how the funds will be used and the expected timeline.]

clauses.title: Financial Projections
clauses.rationale: The lead-in paragraph for the computed table that follows it — states plainly that the numbers are the business owner's own estimates, not a forecast this engine is making or checking.
clauses.body: The table below shows {{company}}'s projected revenue, expenses, and net income. These are estimates prepared by {{company}}, not a guarantee or a professional forecast — [note the key assumptions behind them, such as customer growth rate, pricing, or hiring plan].

clauses.title: Risks
clauses.rationale: Offered rather than automatic — naming the real risks to a plan is the business owner's judgement call, and some plans (an internal-only draft, for instance) skip it.
clauses.body: [Identify the two or three biggest risks to this plan and how {{company}} intends to address them.]
